summary: Client only. Shows your own pages on the game's reading screen, on this machine. Pages use the game's book markup. Events are bookOpened, bookClosed with the reason 'player', 'script', 'failed' or 'sessionOver', and bookTextChanged and bookWritingEnded while the player writes.

open.summary: Opens a book and returns its id. Returns null if there is no body yet, a book is already open, or the player cannot read here; see lastFailure.

params.options: `pages`, required, a list of page texts; `style`, 'book' (default), 'plainBook' or 'letter'; `type`, 1 to 6; `visual`, 1 to 7, the cover; `legibility`, 0 to 1, default 1, how much the character can read; `images`, [{ page, image }], with names from Book.image.

open.exampleLua:
-- client
local Book = kcds.ui.Book

local bookId = Book.open({ style = "letter", pages = { "To the burgrave,\nthe grain did not arrive." } })
if bookId == nil then
  print(Book.lastFailure())
end

close.summary: Closes the open book. Returns false if none is open.

setReadable.summary: Changes how much of the open book the character can read.

setPages.summary: Replaces the open book's pages while it is being read.
setPages.example:
// client
kcds.ui.Book.setPages(['To the burgrave,\nthe grain arrived after all.']);
setPages.exampleLua:
-- client
kcds.ui.Book.setPages({ "To the burgrave,\nthe grain arrived after all." })
setPages.exampleCs:
// client
Book.SetPages(new[] { "To the burgrave,\nthe grain arrived after all." });

write.summary: Lets the player write on a page of the open book, by default the last. Text appears as typed, Enter starts a new line, and Esc ends writing, as does write(false).

currentBook.summary: The open book's id, or null.
currentBook.exampleLua:
-- client
local Book = kcds.ui.Book

if Book.currentBook() ~= nil then
  Book.close()
end

lastFailure.summary: Why the last open() failed, or '' if it did not.
lastFailure.exampleLua:
-- client
local Book = kcds.ui.Book

if Book.open({ pages = { "..." } }) == nil then
  print(Book.lastFailure())
end

image.summary: Makes a .dds your resource ships usable as a page picture, and returns its name for `images`.

params.path: The file's path in your resource.

image.exampleLua:
-- client
local Book = kcds.ui.Book

local crest = Book.image("ui/crest.dds")
Book.open({ style = "letter", pages = { "By order of the burgrave" }, images = { { page = 0, image = crest } } })
